power-profiles-daemon is running: it sets the governor and EPP itself, so an EPP or governor write here lasts only until its next profile change
findings.why: power-profiles-daemon's README (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/upower/power-profiles-daemon, 'Operations on Intel-based machines'): on intel_pstate in active mode it applies the selected profile through the governor and the energy-performance hints. Either keep it and pick its performance profile (powerprofilesctl set performance), or stop it for a benchmark run so EPP writes stick

findings.text: turbo enabled (no_turbo=0)
max_perf_pct=100, min_perf_pct=16
hwp_dynamic_boost=0
findings.why: when 1, a task waking from I/O wait gets a short min-P-state boost; it can help request handlers that block on the network or disk. Unmeasured for inference here — benchmark before keeping it

findings.text: enabled idle states with >=100 us exit latency: C2_ACPI/127us C3_ACPI/1048us
findings.why: a core woken from these pays that latency before it runs; disabling them trims tail latency at the cost of idle power. The 100 us cut-off is this tool's heuristic, not a kernel rule. Runtime disable needs no reboot (intel_idle.max_cstate does)

findings.text: TCC activation 95 C (TjMax 100 C - TCC offset 5 C); package now 95 C

findings.apply: none on the host: improve cooling (airflow, heatsink, BIOS fan or thermal profile); the host-side lever is a lower PL1, see CPU package power limits
findings.text: package thermally throttled 4% of uptime: 22190052 events, 101915027 ms in total, longest 417 ms; core events peak at 8502475 on cpu8
findings.why: therm_throt counts each time the package raised its thermal or PROCHOT status; while it is set the cores run below the frequency they request, so sustained inference speed follows the cooler, not the clock settings. The 1%-of-uptime cut-off is this tool's heuristic

findings.text: MSR 0x1B1 IA32_PACKAGE_THERM_STATUS 0x000000008805080b: now thermal; logged thermal, PROCHOT, power limit; 5 C below TjMax
MSR 0x19C IA32_THERM_STATUS (CPU 0) 0x00000000880b2a88: now none; logged PROCHOT, threshold #1, threshold #2, power limit, current limit; 11 C below TjMax
MSR 0x64F MSR_CORE_PERF_LIMIT_REASONS 0x0000000019030002: now thermal; logged PROCHOT, thermal, other (electrical), PL2, max turbo limit
the log bits are sticky: the SDM says they stay set until software writes 0, so they cover the time since boot or the last clear. doctor --perf only reads them
intel-rapl:0 package-0: PL1 117 W is 3.3x the 35 W thermal spec power while the package is thermally throttled 4% of uptime (long_term 117 W, short_term 117 W, peak_power 230 W)
findings.why: PL1 is the sustained package power. Set above what the cooler removes, it never binds: the package runs into its TCC point and throttles on temperature instead (see CPU thermal throttling). A PL1 the cooler can hold trades peak clocks for steady ones. 2x the thermal spec power is this tool's first step for a sweep, not an Intel figure: measure tokens/s at each step before keeping one. Firmware may re-apply its own value on reboot

findings.apply: sudo mkdir -p /mnt/k3d-gpu-models && sudo mount -t tmpfs -o huge=within_size,size=<model GiB + 1>G tmpfs /mnt/k3d-gpu-models
findings.text: root filesystem is ext4 on Linux 6.6.128-1-MANJARO: model files mmapped from it are mapped with 4 KiB pages, whatever THP enabled says
findings.why: on this kernel ext4 page cache holds no large folios (fs/ext4/inode.c calls mapping_set_large_folios from 6.16), and khugepaged collapses file pages only in executable mappings (include/linux/huge_mm.h file_thp_enabled needs VM_EXEC). OpenVINO and llama.cpp mmap weights by default, so THP covers only anonymous copies. A tmpfs with huge=within_size serves the weights from huge pages (docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/mm/transhuge.html, hugepages in tmpfs/shmem); copy the model in and point the server at it

findings.text: HugePages_Total=0, free 0
MemTotal 125.4 GiB, MemAvailable 61.2 GiB, swap 187.5 GiB, vm.swappiness=60
107.6 GiB of swap in use — the host is under memory pressure
findings.why: anything a server keeps in anonymous memory (KV cache, runtime buffers, weights it copied) is paged back from disk when touched. Free memory or serve a smaller model before benchmarking; MemAvailable is too small to pull the swapped pages back in right now

findings.text: pass --model-gb <size> (or K3D_GPU_MODEL_GB) to check a model against MemAvailable
4x DDR5 SODIMM 32 GiB 2R, ECC (80/64-bit): rated 4800 MT/s, configured 3600 MT/s; 4 of 4 slots populated
SODIMMs at 2 slots per channel are not a supported configuration on the 13th Gen Core S line (743844 table 25 note 9); the nearest POR row, UDIMM 2DPC, 2 DIMMs 2R, is 3600 MT/s
configured 3600 MT/s is at the 3600 MT/s POR for 2DPC, 2 DIMMs 2R
at one module per channel these modules would run at 4800 MT/s (the lower of rated 4800 and the 1DPC 2R POR): 76.8 GB/s peak, with 2 of the 4 modules (less capacity)
peak DRAM bandwidth 57.6 GB/s = 2 channels x 3600 MT/s x 8 B (computed; CPU and iGPU decode share it)

findings.text: 0000:02:00.0 [10de:28b0]: device Gen4 x8, upstream port 0000:00:06.0 Gen4 x4: the link trains at most Gen4 x4
findings.why: a link trains to the lower speed and width of its two ends. current_link_* reads lower at idle (link power management), so only max_* is compared. Keep this GPU's weights and KV cache resident (nothing streamed over the link) and give the widest link to the GPU that moves the most data

sections.good: cores ramp to full turbo the moment a request arrives: EPP performance or balance_performance, turbo on, no frequency caps — token generation is a latency-bound loop and every ramp-up shows in time-to-first-token
sections.name: CPU frequency (driver intel_pstate, mode active)

sections.good: for latency-critical serving, no idle state whose exit latency is large next to a token step; for throughput or power budgets, leave them all on
sections.name: CPU idle states (intel_idle, intel_idle.max_cstate=9)

sections.good: no throttle time under load: the package stays below its TCC activation point (TjMax minus the TCC offset), so cores keep the frequency they request
sections.name: CPU thermal throttling
sections.src: kernel source drivers/thermal/intel/therm_throt.c (thermal_throttle/*), drivers/thermal/intel/int340x_thermal/processor_thermal_device.c (tcc_offset_degree_celsius), drivers/hwmon/coretemp.c (tempN_crit = TjMax), Intel SDM vol. 4 335592-093 (IA32_THERM_STATUS 19CH, IA32_PACKAGE_THERM_STATUS 1B1H, MSR_CORE_PERF_LIMIT_REASONS 64FH in table 2-39)

sections.good: PL1 (long_term) at or above the thermal spec power (TDP, reported as constraint_0_max_power_uw) so sustained inference is not clamped below spec; PL1 decides the clock under a long run, PL2 only covers short bursts. On a package that thermally throttles, a PL1 far above TDP only moves the limit from power to temperature

sections.src: https://docs.kernel.org/power/powercap/powercap.html, kernel source drivers/powercap/intel_rapl_common.c (PL1 max_power = PKG_POWER_INFO thermal spec power)

sections.good: enabled = always or madvise (fewer TLB misses over multi-GB weight and KV buffers), defrag != always (no allocation stalls mid-request)
sections.name: Transparent huge pages

sections.good: 0 unless a server is configured to use hugetlbfs — reserved pages cannot be used for anything else, and OpenVINO, PyTorch and llama.cpp do not use them by default
sections.name: Reserved huge pages (hugetlbfs)

sections.good: the model plus KV cache fits in MemAvailable with headroom and nothing is swapped; swapped-out buffers fault back in at random-I/O speed

sections.good: modules at the platform's plan-of-record (POR) speed for how the slots are populated; single-stream CPU and iGPU decode is bound by DRAM bandwidth. Memory errors counted by an EDAC driver

sections.good: off (run=0, the kernel default) on a node that runs other tenants' pods: merged pages are shared copy-on-write, and the write fault on a merged page is a timing signal another tenant can observe
sections.name: Kernel samepage merging (KSM)
sections.src: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/mm/ksm.html, Suzaki et al., Memory Deduplication as a Threat to the Guest OS, EuroSec 2011

sections.good: irqbalance running, so interrupt load (NIC, NVMe, GPU) is spread over CPUs instead of piling onto the cores that serve tokens

sections.good: each GPU's link trains at the device's own maximum (its upstream port is not slower or narrower), and the large BAR maps all of VRAM (Resizable BAR)
